subject: Polity
description: Governor: appointment, tenure, powers, discretion, removal

questions.stem: GOVERNOR of a STATE is APPOINTED by:
questions.explanation: Article 155 — Governor APPOINTED by PRESIDENT (de facto on Cabinet's advice — typically Home Ministry recommends, PM approves). Holds office during PLEASURE OF PRESIDENT (no fixed term; 5 yrs is normal but can be removed earlier). Article 153 — there shall be a Governor for each STATE. 7th Amendment 1956 → SAME PERSON can be Governor of MULTIPLE states. INSIGHT: although called 'state's' executive, Governor is CENTRE'S nominee → causes federal tension; SARKARIA (1988) + PUNCHHI (2010) Commissions recommended Governors should NOT be active politicians, consult CM, etc. — often violated in practice. APPOINTMENT criteria (Art 157): citizen of India + 35 yrs old. Convention: not a state native (to maintain neutrality). LT. GOVERNOR — for some UTs (Delhi, Puducherry, J&K, Ladakh, A&N).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: MINIMUM AGE qualification for Governor of a state is:
questions.explanation: Article 157 — Governor must: (a) be Indian citizen; (b) be ≥ 35 years old. SAME age as President + Vice President. INSIGHT — PARALLEL OFFICES: Article 153 + 154 — Governor as state's executive head; Article 163 — Council of Ministers to AID + ADVISE Governor (analogous to Pres-PM at centre). Key DIFFERENCES from President: (1) Governor APPOINTED by Pres (Pres elected); (2) Governor has DISCRETIONARY powers in some cases (Article 163 — discretion; Pres has none post-42nd Amendment); (3) Governor can be transferred / removed at any time; Pres can only be impeached. CONVENTIONS — Governor not from same state, not active politician (often broken).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Governor's PARDONING POWER (Article 161) does NOT extend to:
questions.explanation: Governor (Art 161) can PARDON, COMMUTE, REMIT, REPRIEVE for offences against STATE LAWS — but: (a) CANNOT pardon DEATH SENTENCES (only PRESIDENT can; Art 72); (b) CANNOT pardon COURT-MARTIAL cases (only Pres). MERCY petitions for death go to Pres. Compare PRESIDENT (Art 72): can pardon any offence under Union law, court-martial, death sentences. So PRES has WIDER pardoning power than Governor. KOEHLER vs STATE OF ORISSA (1956) — clarified state-Pres pardoning division. INSIGHT — Pres / Governor pardoning is NOT a judicial review; it's an executive grace. Also: NABAM REBIA case (2016, SC, Arunachal) — limited Governor's discretionary powers further; he must act on CM's advice except in defined situations.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Governor APPOINTS the CHIEF MINISTER of the state. CM is:

options.option_text: Leader of majority party in state assembly
Always the senior-most MLA from any party
Person directly elected by state's voters

questions.explanation: CM = LEADER of majority party / coalition in STATE ASSEMBLY. Governor APPOINTS (mostly ceremonial; conventionally invites majority leader). DISCRETION used when no clear majority — Governor can use judgement (notable: Karnataka 2018, Maharashtra 2019 — both controversial). CM holds office during PLEASURE OF GOVERNOR (= until loses confidence in Assembly). NABAM REBIA (2016) limited Governor's power to dismiss CM with floor-test confirmation. CM must be MLA / MLC; if not, must become one within 6 months. Articles 163 + 164 govern state Council of Ministers. Compare CENTRE: PM appointed by Pres similarly; same logic.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: PRESIDENT'S RULE in a state (Article 356) is imposed when:

options.option_text: Governor reports state's constitutional machinery has FAILED
CM resigns from his post for any reason (option here)
Floods / natural disasters strike that state
State demands more central funds urgently (option here)

questions.explanation: Article 356 (President's Rule) — invoked when Governor reports (or Pres satisfied) that STATE GOVT cannot function as per Constitution (e.g., loss of majority, communal riots, breakdown of law + order). Pres takes over state's functions; legislative powers go to Parliament. INITIAL PERIOD: 6 months. Extendable up to 3 YEARS with parliamentary approval (every 6 months). HISTORY — used extensively (often controversially). Most P-Rule states: UP, Bihar, Punjab. CONTROVERSY: BOMMAI CASE (1994) — SC limited misuse, made it judicially reviewable. 'Floor test' must be done in Assembly before dismissal of state govt. Article 365 — refusal to comply with central directives can trigger. Distractor 1 (CM resignation) → Governor invites alternative leader, NOT President's Rule directly.

questions.stem: Salary of GOVERNOR is charged on the:

options.option_text: Consolidated Fund of the state (no Pres veto)
Special trust fund of state legislature

questions.explanation: Governor's SALARY + ALLOWANCES = CHARGED on CONSOLIDATED FUND of the STATE (Article 202(3)) — i.e., paid by the state, NOT central govt. NOT subject to vote of state legislature → ensures financial INDEPENDENCE. (Just discussed, not voted upon.) CURRENT salary: ~₹3.5 lakh/month + allowances (raised from ₹1.10 lakh in 2018). Compare: PRESIDENT (~₹5 lakh/month, charged on Consolidated Fund of INDIA); CJI similar. INSIGHT — 'CHARGED' expenditure (also includes salaries of judges, Speaker, CAG, AG) is NON-VOTABLE — protected from political pressure. Voted expenditure (most other) needs annual parliamentary approval via Appropriation Bill.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Governor of MORE THAN ONE state is permissible per:
questions.explanation: 7th AMENDMENT (1956) — among other things, allowed SAME PERSON to be appointed Governor of TWO OR MORE states. Done to handle small states + special situations. EXAMPLES: Governor of Punjab often Administrator of Chandigarh too; sometimes one Governor handles multiple NE states. CONTEXT — 7th Amendment also implemented STATES REORGANISATION ACT 1956 (linguistic states), abolished classification of states (Part A, B, C, D), redesigned framework. KEY AMENDMENTS to remember: 1st (1951, land reforms, 9th Schedule); 7th (1956, states reorg); 42nd (1976, 'mini-Constitution', Emergency-era); 44th (1978, undid Emergency excesses); 73rd-74th (1992, Panchayats + Municipalities); 86th (2002, Right to Education); 91st (2003, anti-defection); 101st (2016, GST); 103rd (2019, EWS reservation).
